$comment: The gate matrix. One object per gate the close driver knows, plus the two allocator checks and the one open-time refusal that stop a collision before a close ever runs. test/gate-matrix-test.mjs asserts every column here is a real CLOSE-row column in src/lib/lanes.mjs, every tested_in file exists, and every verdicts set equals the literal strings the named source can write. A row whose column is null is enforced but never stored as its own ledger field; a failing value reaches the ledger only inside the CLOSE row's reason text. Where a value below is a judgment rather than a reading of the source, the note says so.

source_forms.function: the body of a top-level function in file, from its declaration to the first line holding only a closing brace
source_forms.const: one exported constant declaration in file, such as LIVE_YES
source_forms.between: the text of file between two comment markers, for a gate measured inline in main()
source_forms.line_contains: every line of file carrying this exact text; used where the driver writes a fixed value

gates.name: merged
gates.what_it_proves: Every path the branch touched holds the same bytes on origin/main as on the branch, compared blob by blob against the merge base, so a squash merge still reads as merged.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That main still builds with a neighbour's work merged beside these files, or that the bytes are correct; a path main edited after the branch started grades no with that path named, not a verdict either way.
gates.note: The pure decision (classifyPath, gradeMerge) is tested; the git-reading wrapper gateMerged is not exported and has no test of its own. n/a is written for a branchless in-place lane on a target that is not a git repository.

gates.name: green
gates.what_it_proves: The branch contained the base's head when the close ran (its own landing merge excused), and then the repo's build exited 0 in the lane's own checkout, inside the time limit, with no signal, on the dispatcher's machine. That build is npm run build, or the command the repo's own policy row declares in its build column, and the gate's line names which one ran. A stale base grades no with the missing commits named and the build is not run. A timeout or a signal grades no. npm that cannot be resolved without a shell grades skip, naming the paths tried, and so does a declared command that is not on PATH.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That main builds once every open lane lands: the base is measured at close time, so a neighbour that lands after this close is not in the build. Nor that the build is safe to run: it executes the branch's own package.json with the close's permissions and no sandbox.
gates.note: test/build-gate-test.mjs runs the real close driver against a fake npm entry point named by npm_execpath, on macOS, Linux and Windows: exit 0, exit 1 with the tail printed, a hung build killed with its process group (its process tree on Windows) past a 1 second PANDORAS_BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS with the grandchild asserted gone, 1 MB of output capped to the last 64 KB, no npm anywhere, the build running in the lane checkout, and a stale base refused before the build. npm runs as node on npm-cli.js with no shell, resolved from npm_execpath, then beside the running Node, then bare npm on PATH on POSIX only (resolveNpm in src/lib/build.mjs). The fresh-base decision is freshBaseFromRevList in src/lib/close.mjs, over freshBaseVerdict and landingGapVerdict; the driver passes grandfathered as false. test/router-test.mjs covers how gradeGates treats a green value. Judgment: external_dependency is git because the base is read from git before anything runs; the build itself is a child process (npm), which the enum has no word for. The limits: 15 minutes by default, the limit the close already used, overridden by PANDORAS_BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS; the last 64 KB of combined output; SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL 2 seconds later, or on Windows taskkill /pid /T /F by argument array. There is no policy column for either limit: the build column names the command only, as an argument array resolved on PATH, and cannot lengthen a limit or reach a shell (parseBuild in src/lib/policy.mjs, resolveOnPath in src/lib/build.mjs).

gates.name: live
gates.what_it_proves: The proof the repo's verify column in POLICY.md names ran and passed, and the verdict sentence names which one. sha: the JSON field at url plus path names a commit that contains the lane's commit by git ancestry. header: the named response header does the same. string: the liveness row's URL answered 200 within its timeout and the first 1 MB of the body carried the expect string, a yes that calls itself best-effort evidence. script: npm run of the named script exited 0 in the lane checkout. none: n/a, the policy names no proof.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: Under the string form, that the response was this branch's build: the string may have been on main already or served from a cache. Under the script form, anything beyond what the script itself checks. Under the sha and header forms, that a squash-merged lane with no LAND record is live: its branch tip is not contained by main, so it grades no rather than yes. Under none, anything at all.
gates.note: src/lib/liveness.mjs writes the word skipped and gateLive rewrites it to skip before it reaches the grader or the ledger. gateLive dispatches on the repo's verify column (VERIFY1, 2026-09-14): sha calls probeShaEcho with liveShaVerdict and a git ancestry check, header calls probeHeaderEcho with the same ancestry check, string calls probeLiveness on the liveness row (the --proof flag replaces its expect string), script runs npm in the lane checkout and grades with scriptProofVerdict, none writes n/a. Each is compared against laneCommitFor's answer: the LAND record's merge commit, else the branch tip. When the sha or header probe cannot reach its endpoint or reads no commit, the gate keeps that probe's skip or no and never falls back to the string probe. An unknown verify form throws when POLICY.md loads, naming the five valid forms. Still exported, tested and not invoked here: the novelty rule (proofStringNovel), the string form's precedence (liveStringVerdict), the surfaces table (surfaceReach) and the second ask (deployProbePlan). The grader also accepts exempt as a pass and site/gates.html describes it, but no code path in this repository writes exempt. See docs/LIVENESS.md.

gates.name: renamed
gates.what_it_proves: No brief on the bridge whose filename carries this lane's id as a whole hyphen-delimited token still classifies as live under PREFIXES.md, so the next dispatch will not fire it again.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That the brief's work was finished; a lane that renames its own brief passes this gate whatever it shipped.
gates.note: The filename matcher (briefMatchesLaneOrKey) is tested; the directory listing around it is not. With --apply, and only when this is the sole failing gate or the lane's report is already on the bridge, the close itself renames the brief (renameOnCloseVerdict), so the value recorded is the one measured before that rename.

gates.name: in-scope
gates.what_it_proves: Every path the lane's branch touched sits inside the file scope the lane declared when it opened, or on the ALWAYS_IN_SCOPE allowlist, which ships empty; a lane that declared Touches: none touched no path at all. Before the branch is merged the touched paths are its diff against the merge base; once merged they are the paths its own first-parent commits changed since the base recorded at OPEN.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That a change inside the scope cannot break a file outside it through an API shape, a schema, a generated file or a shared constant; the gate measures paths, not effects. On a merged branch, an edit made only inside a merge commit's conflict resolution is not counted, because the walk reads non-merge commits. See docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, entry b.
gates.note: n/a means the lane declared no scope and therefore held the repo alone. skip means a real scope was declared and nothing was measured against it: the lane committed nothing, git could not list the touched paths, or the branch is merged and no base was recorded at OPEN. no names every path outside the declaration; for a Touches: none lane that is every path it touched (inScopeVerdict). Which commits are read is scopeDiffPlan: the merge-base diff while the merge base is behind the branch tip, and the first-parent walk from the recorded base once the branch is merged or no merge base can be computed. A plain diff from the recorded base was rejected because a lane that brought main in before landing would carry every neighbour's landed file in it and be refused for them. Both readings changed on 2026-09-14; before that a merged branch graded skip and a Touches: none lane that committed files graded n/a. The git reads around these functions are not exported; the decisions are tested in test/router-test.mjs.

gates.name: findings
gates.what_it_proves: Every FINDING: line in the lane's own report names a fix, a valid size and an owner, and no small finding is handed to the human owner.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That the finding is real or the fix is right; the gate polices the shape of the line, never its content.
gates.note: Ledger column `findings` (Router COLUMNS1, 2026-09-14), appended after `kind`; a line written before that reads '-'. n/a is written when the report is not on disk yet, which is the normal order for a lane closing before it writes up.

gates.name: no-side-files
gates.what_it_proves: No REFERENCE-, SWEEP- or TRIAGE- file modified on the bridge between the lane's OPEN stamp and now can be attributed to this lane by its body naming the lane or the brief title, or by the lane's own report naming it.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That no side file was written at all: a matching file in the window that none of the attribution tests tie to this lane prints a warning and passes.
gates.note: Ledger column `side-files` (Router COLUMNS1, 2026-09-14), appended after `kind`; a line written before that reads '-'. This driver passes no worktreeDiffPaths, so the attribution test that reads the lane's branch diff never fires here; only the body and report tests do. A Side-file: allowed line in the brief header makes the gate n/a, and a lane with no recorded open time reads skip.

gates.name: report-free
gates.what_it_proves: Nothing at close: this driver writes the literal n/a on every close, which the grader counts as a pass.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That the report filename was free; the check that would prove it (reportFreeVerdict, tested) is never called by this driver.
gates.note: The collision this gate was built for is handled earlier: the allocator numbers a taken name (row report-name-collision) and hooks/guard-report-overwrite.mjs refuses a whole-file Write onto an existing bridge report at run time.

gates.name: owner-way-in
gates.what_it_proves: Nothing: the driver hands the grader no value, which gradeGates reads as n/a, and writes the dash to the ledger, which every reader treats as not measured.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That the owner's stored credential still opens the deployment; no code in this repository performs that check.
gates.note: The grader's handling of a supplied owner-way-in value (no leads the reason line; skip fails; n/a passes) is tested in test/router-test.mjs. The measurement itself has no implementation here.

gates.name: roadmap
gates.what_it_proves: Nothing: same shape as owner-way-in, the grader sees n/a and the ledger gets a dash.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That the brief names a board row; the verdict that would say so lives outside this repository.
gates.note: gradeGates grades a supplied roadmap value and test/router-test.mjs covers that grading; nothing in this repository produces one.

gates.name: scope-disjoint
gates.what_it_proves: Two lanes offered to run together in one repo declared file scopes that share no path after normalisation, exclusive-path widening, and the whole-repo default for anything undeclared or unparseable; a held claim with no OPEN record counts as the whole repo.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That the two lanes cannot break one another through a shared interface; disjoint paths mean no two lanes write one file, and nothing more. See docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, entry b.
gates.note: Not a close gate and not a verdict word: the outcome is a card that either fires now or carries a firesAfter sentence naming the lane and the overlapping paths. The verdicts list is empty on purpose and the matrix test checks only that the named functions exist. The shell (src/bin/lane-alloc.mjs) reads disk and ledger; allocate itself is pure.

gates.name: report-name-collision
gates.what_it_proves: The report filename printed on a card carries the lane id and was not already on the bridge at allocation time; a taken name gets a numbered variant and the card says so.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That two sessions of one lane cannot collide after allocation: both derive the same name, and the runtime defence is hooks/guard-report-overwrite.mjs, not this check.
gates.note: Not a close gate. The card field is reportTaken, a boolean, so the verdicts list is empty on purpose. Judgment: external_dependency is none because allocate is pure and is handed the set of existing report names; the shell that builds that set lists the bridge directory, so a reader who counts the shell would say filesystem.

gates.name: checkout-unexplained
gates.what_it_proves: An existing checkout directory at the lane's derived path is either this lane's own PARTIAL leftover, which the open resumes, or unexplained, which the open refuses as a collision.
gates.what_it_does_not_prove: That no session is inside a directory the ledger explains; a lane with an OPEN record and no CLOSE is refused precisely because its folder existing proves nothing either way.
gates.note: Judgment: the brief asked for the two allocator rows; this open-time refusal is added because it is the third place a collision is stopped before a close, and without it the enforced_by value open would name nothing.

close_refusals.$comment: Not gates. A failing gate makes the close PARTIAL and the close still happens, while these three abort it with a non-zero exit and write nothing, on a dry run as well. Decided by doneReportRefusal in src/lib/close.mjs and reached through closeReportRefusal, which src/bin/close.mjs calls whenever the lane's report is on disk, whatever the gates graded.
close_refusals.note: All three can fire in this driver. closeReportRefusal reads the report through report-check's own checks (checkText in src/lib/report-check.mjs) and hands doneReportRefusal present: true, statusFound, the STATUS word, the Evidence answer, the done-honest WARN with its flagged lines, and whether an overruled: line names report-check. That is the shape of the private workspace close's call. A report report-check reads as a consumed brief is never refused and the close prints a note saying so; no report on disk yet refuses nothing. Until 2026-09-14 the driver called doneReportRefusal without present and with doneHonestWarn fixed at false, so none of the three could fire; test/router-test.mjs now drives each refusal through closeReportRefusal with real report text, and the matrix test turns red if the driver stops passing presence.

ledger.$comment: The CLOSE record as recordClose writes it. The RECORD FORMS comment at the top of src/lib/lanes.mjs lists the columns through roadmap and omits kind; the HEADER that file writes into a fresh LANES.md stops at owner-way. recordClose is the authority, and the matrix test reads the comment line and then checks recordClose for the appended field.
